name: Abihail
overview: Abihail is a male biblical figure known primarily as the father of Hadassah (Esther) and the uncle of Mordecai, as recorded in Esther 2:15. There is no additional information about his tribal affiliation or other distinguishing notes. His role is significant within the family context of key figures in the Book of Esther.
namesAndTitles: The name Abihail is a proper name meaning '[my] father has strength/wealth or cause of strength/wealth.' This meaning reflects a name of strength or provision, though it is not indicated that the name was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Abihail as the father of Hadassah (Esther) and the uncle of Mordecai, establishing his place within this notable family lineage. Beyond these relationships, no further family details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Abihail's significance lies in his familial connection to Esther and Mordecai, two central figures in the biblical narrative of deliverance found in the Book of Esther. As Esther's father and Mordecai's uncle, he is part of the ancestral background that situates these key characters within God's providential plan. His mention helps anchor the genealogy and heritage of those who played vital roles in God's preservation of His people.
